1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is not naturally occurring in the cell.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo from heterologous nucleic acid encoding the at least one BMC polypeptide.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme that is not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in the cell.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes from heterologous sources.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence that directs localization of the enzyme to the non-native compartment.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide from a bacterial species different from the host cell species.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides that are not all naturally co-expressed in the host cell.

9. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons that are not naturally present together in the host cell.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag for purification or detection of the non-native compartment.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide that is heterologous to the host cell, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is not naturally occurring in the untransformed host cell.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium that does not naturally contain the BMC polypeptide being introduced.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae that does not naturally express the introduced BMC polypeptide.

17. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast.

18. (Original) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae.

19. (Original) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga that does not naturally contain the BMC polypeptide being introduced.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide that is heterologous to the cell, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product within the non-native compartment; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product, wherein the conversion is enhanced by compartmentalization within the non-native compartment.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product that is produced at higher levels or with greater efficiency than in cells lacking the non-native compartment.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate by sequestering the substrate or intermediates within the non-native compartment.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments from the cell.

27. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of non-native compartments that are not naturally present in the cell.
